category_title: Boys who have been victims of bullying and project parental advice into social interactions
scenario_title: Role-play discussion on victim's feelings and coping strategies
minimal_context: The student is participating in a one-on-one role-play activity using a scarf to compare the feelings of a bully and a victim and offer advice.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: For this part of our role-play, I am going to put on this scarf and pretend to be the victim. How do you think the victim is feeling right now?

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: His feelings are fear, loneliness, pain, sadness, hatred towards the bully and humiliation. He has no support from other children, so he cannot talk to anyone since nobody could really understand how he is feeling.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: What about the bully? What could the bully do to solve the problem he created?

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: Apology would be the right thing to do in order to find a way out of his problem but at the same time it would be a mistake since by apologising he would show weakness and nobody would hold him in high esteem anymore.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Let's go back to the victim. What advice would you give to the victim to handle this situation?

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: He needs help. I would certainly become his friend. I would tell him to believe and trust himself. I would tell him to do whatever he likes and not to be afraid of other people... he has to believe that he can make it. Suppression of anger is the only way to deal with the problem, even though that is difficult without help from someone outside.

TUTOR: What about the bully? What could the bully do to solve the problem he created?

STUDENT: Apology would be the right thing to do in order to find a way out of his problem but at the same time it would be a mistake since by apologising he would show weakness and nobody would hold him in high esteem anymore.

TUTOR: Let's go back to the victim. What advice would you give to the victim to handle this situation?
